items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-09
items.q: Before Buddy Baldwin was an old man, so-and-so way back then, probably old man Merritt. That's generations.

ctx.x: Do you think there are different kinds of jazz? He said he spoke about American jazz with his friends and German jazz.

Well, we don't look at it that way. I mean, when I play with them boys, they sound the same as anybody over here. I'm just saying that. And then... You mean the copy? How do we know who copy? Who we... Who, how... For generations, before my time was Joe Oliver. I was mine. Of course, there was other good ones, but I'm just narrating it down. And before Joe Oliver's time was Buddy Baldwin. Before Buddy Baldwin was an old man, so-and-so way back then, probably old man Merritt. That's generations. Now, how we know…
While you were down in Caracas, did you by any chance happen to get in personal contact with, uh, uh, some of our band leaders and musicians? I played on the TV there. Yeah.
